verdict.rationale: npm's own docs say it can be pointed at any compatible registry, including a self-hosted one, and can install from a different registry than the one the lock file was made with. That is a documented way to extend it with third-party backends, and the community corroborates it (Verdaccio as a self-hosted registry, switching registries via `npm config set`). There is no evidence of a plugin, tap, or overlay mechanism that extends the manager's own behavior. Missing for 10: a plugin or extension system for the CLI itself, tap or overlay-style package sources, and in-depth docs on the registry backend protocol.

support.subject: As a developer, I can extend the manager through third-party taps, overlays, plugins, or backends

citations.quote: You can configure npm to use any compatible registry you like, and even run your own registry.
If you create a lock file while using the default registry you can switch to another registry and npm will install packages from the new registry
Verdaccio exists as a self-hosted npm registry alternative
